summary: Mohnish Pabrai argues that humans have an evolutionary aversion to cloning, preferring to follow the crowd rather than adopt proven mental models or business structures. He illustrates this by noting that despite Warren Buffett's highly successful fee structure ending in 1969, no one successfully cloned that specific model for thirty years until Ben Watsa did so, demonstrating that simple, effective ideas are often undervalued because people underestimate their importance and overestimate the need for complexity.
